gloss: to prepare; to get ready; to make preparations

definitions.gloss: to prepare; to get ready; to make preparations
definitions.explanation: To arrange or organize things in advance so that one is ready for a future event, task, or situation.

examples.japanese: {旅行|りょこう}の{準備|じゅんび}をする。
{明日|あした}の{会議|かいぎ}の{資料|しりょう}を{準備|じゅんび}した。
examples.english: I prepared the materials for tomorrow's meeting.

examples.japanese: {災害|さいがい}に{備|そな}えて、{非常食|ひじょうしょく}や{水|みず}を{準備|じゅんび}しておいたほうがいい。
examples.english: You should prepare emergency food and water in case of a disaster.

notes:
One of the most frequently used verbs in daily Japanese. Used broadly for any kind of advance preparation, from packing for a trip to setting up a meeting room. Often takes the pattern {準備|じゅんび}をする (with を particle) as well as {準備|じゅんび}する.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {準備|じゅんび}が{整|ととの}う: preparations are complete
- {準備|じゅんび}ができる: to be ready
- {準備|じゅんび}{不足|ぶそく}: lack of preparation
- {準備|じゅんび}{期間|きかん}: preparation period
- {心|こころ}の{準備|じゅんび}: mental preparation

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {用意|ようい}する: to prepare / to arrange — focuses on having things ready and at hand; more concrete and immediate
- {支度|したく}する: to get ready — focuses on personal preparation like getting dressed or packing
- {備|そな}える: to prepare for / to provide against — emphasizes precaution against future events

USAGE:
{準備|じゅんび}する is the most general and versatile preparation verb. It works for both concrete tasks (preparing materials) and abstract contexts (preparing mentally). {用意|ようい}する is more about having specific items ready, while {準備|じゅんび}する covers the broader process of getting ready.
